item.title: Lucayan staff five weeks’ unpaid for a second time
item.description: Grand Lucayan staff have gone five weeks without pay for a second time, it has been confirmed, with the resort now owing a total $17m to its Bahamian and international suppliers and other creditors.

item.title: Around da Islands: The Tribune and GB 242 News launch media partnership
item.description: The Tribune today announces a new media partnership with Grand Bahama 242 News to bring expanded coverage of Grand Bahama and the Family Islands to readers across The Bahamas.

item.title: Coleby-Davis: 82% of households saw lower power bills in 2025
item.description: THOUSANDS of households paid at least 15 percent less for electricity in 2025 under the Equity Rate Adjustment (ERA) programme, Energy and Transport Minister JoBeth Coleby-Davis told the House of Assembly yesterday, saying the tariff reform is already delivering measurable savings for consumers.

item.title: Bowleg ‘unbothered’ by Rick Fox ratification for Garden Hills seat
item.description: GARDEN Hills MP Mario Bowleg appeared unbothered yesterday after former NBA player Rick Fox was ratified as the Free National Movement’s candidate for the constituency.

item.title: Broken neck suffered in illegal ‘Uber’ ride
item.description: A CRASH that left a Grand Bahama preschool teacher with a broken neck and torn eyelids has thrown fresh light on what officials have described as a dangerous regulatory vacuum around ride-sharing services operating in The Bahamas, some falsely claiming to be “Uber” drivers.

item.title: Davis calls Pintard ‘stupid’ during House energy debate
item.description: PRIME Minister Philip Davis called Opposition Leader Michael Pintard “stupid” in the House of Assembly yesterday during a tense debate over the government’s energy reforms and its plan to guarantee credit facilities tied to the country’s liquefied natural gas transition.

item.title: 50/50 labour split for building new hospital
item.description: BAHAMIAN workers will make up 50 percent of the construction workforce for the $268 million speciality hospital on the Perpall Tract, Health and Wellness Minister Michael Darville told the House of Assembly yesterday.

item.title: Darville: Ministry will call up 47 retired nurses as they look to recruit 50 more from Ghana
item.description: HEALTH Minister Michael Darville said 47 retired nurses will re-enter the public healthcare system next month and the government is in the final stages of recruiting 50 Ghanaian nurses with specialised skills.
